transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 15:00 PT | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Partnerships); Rajiv Patel (Velascale), Elena Korsakov (Velascale), Tom Nguyen (Velascale SE), Sara Lee (Velascale Legal)

Summary: Quick intros -> partner program + technical integration possibilities. Talked hardware SKUs, on-prem and cloud flows, marketplace listing, compliance items (SOC2, SSO), and pilot scope.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood, im the AE on this. quick round-robin?
[00:12] Rajiv Patel: Hi all, Rajiv here, head of partnerships at Velascale. we do custom GPU blades, partner marketplace and managed infra for ML customers.
[00:24] Elena Korsakov: Elena, run cloud ops at Velascale, want to understand how Redwood would integrate with our stack.
[00:31] Tom Nguyen: Tom, solutions eng. i'll be the tech point, want to dig into runtime and perf expectations.
[00:38] Lucas Ortega: Lucas, Redwood SE, focusing on inference runtime, batching, kv cache, quantization profiles etc.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Great. goal today: intro, high level partnership models (reseller/marketplace/integration), and surface technical blockers. we'll capture next steps at the end.

[02:10] Rajiv Patel: Quick q — what partner motions have you done with, like, cloud vendors? are you doing marketplace images or managed service?
[02:23] Priya Nair: We do both — hosted API and dedicated / private deployments. for partners like you we usually do a combined approach: marketplace images for quick onboarding + dedicated/managed offer for larger customers.
[02:40] Rajiv Patel: Ok understood. commercial curiosity — margins vs rev share, do you have standard tiers?
[02:52] Maya Chen: We have a partner tiering doc — revenue share for marketplace-based referrals, reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated with co-sell pricing. i'll send the partner playbook after.

[05:15] Tom Nguyen: Techwise, our customers care about throughput for L2-L3 models and also about latency for chatty agents. what does Redwood runtime look like on your side?
[05:30] Lucas Ortega: Runtime is GPU-optimized with continuous batching, kv cache handling, and kernel selection that adapts to sequence length. we also support quantized variants — that lets you squeeze more perf on a given SKU.
[05:48] Tom Nguyen: Nice. any pref hardware? like do you support A100, H100, and the newer Vela chipsets?
[05:58] Lucas Ortega: We support common NVIDIA SKUs (A100/H100) out of the box; for custom vendor chips we onboard model kernels — sometimes we need kernel work or compilation flags. for your Vela silicon we can onboard but will need perf validation.

[07:05] Elena Korsakov: On security, our customers require SOC 2 and SSO/SAML integration and kms for keys. can Redwood run in our VPC/on-prem?
[07:15] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem. we integrate with KMS/HSM and provide audit logs and RBAC. we'll share our compliance pack.

[09:40] Rajiv Patel: From a go-to-market Srategy, we want a simple flow: 1) list a marketplace image, 2) offer managed deployments, 3) co-sell for bigger deals. do you have experience with cloud marketplaces?
[09:55] Priya Nair: Yes — we have AWS and GCP marketplace listings and a template onboarding flow. marketplace installs can spin up Dedicated or private agents depending on customer preference.

[12:05] Tom Nguyen: For benchmarks — do you have a standard harness we can run on Vela hardware? cpu vs gpu comparisons?
[12:15] Lucas Ortega: We'll provide a benchmark template and perf checklist. it includes token/sec, p95 latency, memory/KV cache metrics. note: transcription — sorry, memory K-V cash, uh kv-cache.

[14:00] Rajiv Patel: Are there known issues with batching on multi-tenant Dedicated pools? some vendors worry about noisy neighbors and perf variance.
[14:12] Lucas Ortega: Our dedicated pools are pool-isolated per customer. we also do pinning and capacity reservations. for shared hosting we have QoS and fallback policies to cheaper model variants.

[16:30] Elena Korsakov: Legal question — we need data residency guarantees and purge policies. do you support tenant-level data retention controls?
[16:40] Maya Chen: Yes, retention controls, purge APIs, and audit logs. also SSO + SCIM integration for enterprise. we'll share SOC2 and our security whitepaper.

[19:00] Rajiv Patel: Commercial terms again — what's typical for reserved capacity? monthly commitments?
[19:12] Maya Chen: Reserved capacity is monthly or annual commits with discounted unit pricing. we can discuss a partner reseller rate for Velascale customers.

[21:22] Tom Nguyen: For model variants and quantization — will Redwood handle compiling optimized kernels for our hardware or do you expect us to provide a runtime?
[21:34] Lucas Ortega: We do the kernel selection and compilation; for novel hardware we may need a small engineering engagement. sometimes we ship a compiled runtime/container for your SKU.

[24:10] Sara Lee: legal — any IP concerns with co-branded images or shared benchmarks?
[24:20] Maya Chen: Typical NDA and partner agreement covers IP and co-marketing. we can put a clause for benchmark data sharing limited to the two parties.

[26:50] Rajiv Patel: ok sounds good. on the risk side, customers ask about graceful degradation and fallbacks — how does Redwood do that?
[27:02] Lucas Ortega: Smart routing and fallbacks — route by latency/cost/region. automatic fallback to smaller model or hosted API if Dedicated capacity constrained.

[29:30] Tom Nguyen: integration points — API surface for deployment, a marketplace image, and telemetry hooks for Console, right?
[29:41] Priya Nair: yes, Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, and can emit logs to partner SIEMs.

[32:00] Rajiv Patel: curious about support model; if a Velascale-managed customer has an infra issue, do you triage or do we?
[32:12] Maya Chen: Typically we do shared ops — triage together. for dedicated/reseller deals we can offer premium SLA and a coordinated runbook.

[34:50] Elena Korsakov: timeline — if we want a pilot with 3 customers, what's realistic? 4-6 weeks?
[35:00] Lucas Ortega: 4-8 weeks depending on kernel work and integration. if it's standard NVIDIA SKUs likely 3-4 weeks; new hardware could push to 6-8 weeks.

[37:20] Rajiv Patel: ok next steps?
[37:25] Maya Chen: I'll recap: Maya to send partner deck & playbook; Lucas to share benchmark template and perf checklist; schedule tech deep dive with Velascale infra (Tom/Elena) week of 3/16; Rajiv to share marketplace onboarding doc and preferred commercial model.

[39:05] Tom Nguyen: a quick nit - we will want a sample deployment manifest and helm chart for your private offering.
[39:14] Lucas Ortega: we'll share a sample helm chart and container image for the marketplace flow.

[41:00] Rajiv Patel: awesome. any final questions?
[41:10] Sara Lee: none from legal right now i think we'll review docs after you send them.
[42:00] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the tech deep-dive.
[42:10] Rajiv Patel: thanks all, excited to explore this.

End of transcript.
